reasoning_trace: Traced hounfour.locality: local_voices from adversarial-review.sh/_adv_locality_filter, flatline_locality_gate and Bridgebuilder applyLocality to the classifier. Every planner decides 'local' from the dispatch_group label alone; endpoint_policy.validate_providers never refuses the label on a provider whose endpoint is a public https host; cheval reads locality only for telemetry (hop_telemetry) and _transport_policy/hop_locality_of read the model entry only. Reproduced with the head classifier and loader against a Together.ai provider labelled local.
finding: The local_voices confidentiality posture is satisfied by a YAML label; a hosted provider labelled dispatch_group: local is planned, dispatched and recorded as local, and the label is read inconsistently (provider-block label honoured by planners, ignored by cheval's transport and MODELINV).
critique: A posture whose guarantee ('the prompt does not cross a public network') is defeated by one key, with an audit row that then says local, is a protection-mechanism failure.
remediation: Define local as a checkable property (HTTP provider, not CLI, endpoint host admitted by check_insecure_optin); refuse dispatch_group: local at load otherwise; resolve the label once (entry else provider block) and share the rule across hop-locality.py, hop_locality_of, _transport_policy, isLocalVoice; enforce in cheval at dispatch time under local_voices.

code_snippet: Since cycle-129 the provider, locality and exit keys follow the trusted-source precedence below even when the checkout is a PR head.
reasoning_trace: loadTrustedConfig (config.ts:605) reads the head only for keyless/insecure booleans (config.ts:684); voices still dispatch through cheval (multi-model-pipeline.ts:224-225) which loads the checkout's .loa.config.yaml; loadMultiModelConfig (config.ts:104) also reads the checkout's file. validate_declared_endpoint admits any https host, verified against the head validator.
finding: The trusted configuration governs only Bridgebuilder's planning; a PR head that keeps a trusted provider's keyless/opt-in flags but changes endpoint, aliases or allowlists is admitted and the prompt (and a {env:VAR} credential) are sent where the head says. The SKILL.md claim overstates the protection.
critique: The control sits in the planner while the dispatcher reads another file.
remediation: On a pull request diff hounfour.providers/aliases/locality/secret_env_allowlist between head and trusted view and refuse on any difference, or pass the trusted config to cheval explicitly; correct SKILL.md; add a test where only endpoint changes.

reasoning_trace: validate_providers admits allow_insecure_endpoint on any non-CLI provider type (reproduced with type: anthropic over http://10.0.0.6). Only OpenAIAdapter builds a TransportPolicy (openai_adapter.py:221); anthropic_adapter.py and google_adapter.py (untouched, framework copy) call http_post_stream without a policy. Cross-model DISS-C-001 confirmed.
finding: The request-time half of D-7.2 (no proxy env, no redirects, path prefix) applies only to OpenAI-type providers, while the load-time half admits the opt-in on every HTTP provider type.
critique: The module docstring (endpoint_policy.py:26-28) promises the request-time rules for 'an opted-in provider'.
remediation: Refuse allow_insecure_endpoint at load unless type is openai/openai_compat (the probe already does), or apply TransportPolicy in every adapter.

reasoning_trace: httpx trust_env=False disables SSL_CERT_FILE/SSL_CERT_DIR as well as proxy discovery; the urllib fallback honours them through OpenSSL. Three sites: base.py:300, 397, 533.
finding: An https local or opted-in hop presenting a private-CA certificate trusted via SSL_CERT_FILE fails verification on hosts with httpx and succeeds without it; operators are nudged toward disabling verification.
critique: Proxies should be disabled without discarding the operator's CA configuration.
remediation: Pass verify=ssl.create_default_context() or disable proxies via proxy=None/mounts instead of trust_env=False; add a self-signed https stub test.

reasoning_trace: rc 3 is converted to exit 0 at :89-90 without checking that bb-stdout.json holds a run JSON; bb-exit-degraded-callers.bats has no exit-3-with-empty-stdout case.
finding: Any exit 3 (a shell error inside entry.sh, a mixed-version dist) is reported as a completed degraded review.
critique: The scheduled contract loses the property that a non-zero exit without a review is a failure.
remediation: Treat 3 as completed-degraded only when jq -e '.verdicts|type=="array"' succeeds on $BB_OUT; otherwise exit 3.

reasoning_trace: validate_providers admits a keyed provider over http to any RFC1918 host (reproduced: http://10.0.0.5 with auth {env:OPENAI_API_KEY}); OpenAIAdapter then sends Authorization: Bearer in cleartext. The example recommends the pattern. Cross-model DISS-C-002 confirmed; severity set LOW because the configuration is explicit and LAN-scoped.
finding: A real credential may travel in cleartext across a LAN to an opted-in http host, with no load-time warning.
critique: The opt-in was designed for keyless local servers; nothing enforces or warns about the pairing.
remediation: WARN at load when an http opt-in provider carries a non-keyless auth; prefer https or loopback-only for keyed providers in the example.

reasoning_trace: The opt-in admits localhost under the claim (:1054, endpoint_policy.py:6) that it is never resolved; httpx/urllib resolve it via the OS resolver at request time and TransportPolicy.check_url never checks the resolved address.
